text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Crown Prince and Prime Minister Sheikh Saad al-Abdulla al-Sabah leaves bed, minister says. Sheikh Saad flew to London on Monday for follow-up treatment after undergoing colon surgery in Kuwait on Saturday.
- Kuwait and Sri Lanka sign agreement to avoid double taxation.

- Armed Iraqi boats violate the dimiltarised zone between Kuwait and Iraq. The United Nations in 1991 declared a border strip a dimilitarised zone after the Gulf War that ended a seven-month Iraqi occupation of Kuwait.
- Investment firms lead active trade at the Kuwait Stock Exchange. Share index up 8.1 points to 2,246.1.
- Two Iranian infiltrators arrested. Many Iranians enter Kuwait illegally to seek higher paying jobs in the tiny oil-rich state.
- Kuwait's imports in the first nine months of 1996 totalled 1.8 billion dinars ($5.9 billion), Commerce and Industry Ministry official says.
- Emir Sheikh Jaber al-Ahmad al-Sabah receives message from Pakistan's President Farooq Leghari.
